cases.invariant: An exact LaTeX alias outranks everything; `\to` is the shortest route to the commonest arrow.
The alias a technical writer already has in their fingers wins over every name match.
An alias no name contains resolves to exactly one character.
SEARCH is case-insensitive, so `phi` reaches both cases; the tie falls in code-point order. Case is respected only on the exact-alias COMMIT path — see findByAlias.
Query case is folded before searching, exactly as it is for emoji.
A whole-name prefix puts the plain character ahead of its 100-odd decorated variants.
A name that matches exactly has no competition.
The punctuation a writer actually hunts for is one query away.
Ties inside one bucket fall in (block, code point) order — Unicode's own layout does the ranking.
The NameAllWords bucket's headline case: ‖ is DOUBLE VERTICAL LINE and reaches this query as a plain prefix, ahead of the turnstiles that merely contain the words.

NameAllWords is what makes `greek phi` reach GREEK SMALL LETTER PHI at all — the words are not adjacent in the name. It ranks below the plain prefix match (ϕ, GREEK PHI SYMBOL), which is the whole point of it being the last bucket.
Each query token claims a DISTINCT name word, so a repeated token needs the name to repeat it too: LEFTWARDS ARROW TO BAR OVER RIGHTWARDS ARROW TO BAR qualifies.

Assignment is greedy, left to right, and NOT a maximum matching. RIGHTWARDS ARROW is absent — its single `right`-prefixed word is taken by the first token. Do not replace this with a backtracking matcher without regenerating both corpora.
